## Helix design-system patterns

<!-- Generated by @cdx/helix-ai@22.0.0-alpha.1 — do not edit by hand. -->

When building UI with the Helix design system (Angular + Material 3), prefer a
documented pattern over inventing a composition, and follow this repo's Angular
baseline. The full reference for each pattern (rules, components, anti-patterns,
example code) is in `.claude/skills/helix-patterns/references/<id>.md`.

| Pattern                | Use when                                                                                                                                                  | Summary                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| AI assistant           | A product's AI chat or assistant surface, full-page or in a side panel.                                                                                   | A conversational assistant: a thread of user and assistant message cards, a streaming answer announced to assistive technology, per-answer feedback, and a docked composer — built on the Helix AI avatar and gradient. |
| AI chat history        | An AI assistant keeps a history of conversations the user returns to, resumes, renames or cleans up.                                                      | A panel of past AI conversations, grouped by recency and titled by their first question, that the user can reopen, rename and delete — with real loading, empty and error states, not just the happy path.              |
| AI entry points        | Deciding how to surface AI in an app shell: the global way in (header, rail, or FAB) and how to announce a new AI capability.                             | Where and how the user reaches AI — a header/rail trigger, a floating action button, and a one-time promo banner — all wearing the same Helix AI treatment so AI is recognisable and leads to one assistant surface.    |
| AI generate & rewrite  | Helping the user write or revise one field or block of text — an alert description, a summary, a note — in place.                                         | A one-shot AI action on a single field — draft, rewrite, shorten, fix — that proposes new text the user reviews and accepts, discards or regenerates, with an undo. Not a conversation.                                 |
| AI generation trace    | An AI answer whose provenance matters — which sources, filters or steps produced it — especially in regulated or high-stakes contexts.                    | A collapsed "How was this generated?" disclosure under an AI answer, showing the steps the assistant took and the inputs it used — so users can understand and trust the result.                                        |
| Inline AI actions      | The user is reading content (a document, a row, a report section) and an AI action on that content would help without leaving the page.                   | Bring the assistant to the content: AI actions (summarise, explain, ask about this) attached to a document or a selection, with the result shown in place or sent to the assistant — not a detour to a separate chat.   |
| AI prompt starters     | The empty state of an AI assistant, before the first message, full-page or in a panel.                                                                    | The pre-conversation landing for an assistant: a short greeting, a few suggested-prompt cards that seed the composer, and the composer itself — so the user isn't facing a blank box.                                   |
| AI sources & citations | An AI answer is grounded in documents and the user must be able to check any statement against its source.                                                | Make an AI answer traceable — number claims with inline citations that reveal the cited passage and link to the source, and list the ranked source documents behind the answer, collapsed past a handful.               |
| AI usage & limits      | An assistant with quotas, a bounded context window, or rate limits — anywhere a request can be refused for a limit rather than an error.                  | Tell the user where they stand against AI limits — responses left, a context that's too long, a rate limit — before and when they hit them, with a clear way forward, using hlx-notification.                           |
| App shell              | The top-level layout of a product. Every routed page renders inside it.                                                                                   | The standard page chrome — Helix header with product name, primary navigation and global actions, a routed content area, and the footer — assembled once and driven by typed route data.                                |
| Charts                 | Visualising quantitative data — trends, comparisons, distributions — in a product screen or dashboard.                                                    | Build charts with the Helix Highcharts styled-mode theme so colour, type and axes come from the design system — never a hardcoded palette — and keep them accessible and readable.                                      |
| Data grid wrapper      | Large, sortable, filterable or column-managed datasets — the results grid in a list page, an analytics table, anything beyond a simple mat-table.         | One place to set up AG Grid the Helix way — modules and licence registered once, a Theming-API theme built from Helix tokens, shared column defaults, and column-state persistence.                                     |
| Dialogs                | Confirming a decision (especially a destructive one), a short focused task, or showing detail beside the current page without navigating away.            | A modal for one decision or one short task. Open it through a named size preset, structure the body with the Material dialog slots, and put the primary action on the right.                                            |
| Entity detail          | The detail view of one record — a drug, a trial, a target — reached from a list or search.                                                                | A record page: an entity header, a summary card of the key facts, then an accordion of sections that load lazily and are disabled when they have nothing to show.                                                       |
| Error pages            | A whole route can't be shown — not found (404), not permitted (403), or a server error (500).                                                             | Full-page states for 404, 403 and 500 — a centred hlx-empty-state with a pictogram, a plain explanation and one clear way forward, served by the router.                                                                |
| Export                 | Letting the user download the current data (a grid, a report) as CSV, Excel or PDF, especially when the file is generated server-side and takes a moment. | An export action: pick a format, then give asynchronous feedback through snackbars — preparing, then ready (or failed with retry) — so the user isn't left staring at a frozen button.                                  |
| Form layout            | Collecting or editing structured input — a settings page, a create/edit form, a filter builder saved as a form.                                           | A single-column form of Material fields grouped into sections, with inline validation on blur, a required/optional convention, and a docked action bar — laid out with Helix spacing tokens.                            |
| List with filters      | Browsing or searching a collection — alerts, documents, drugs, trials — that the user narrows with filters.                                               | A results page: a toolbar with search and filters, the applied filters shown as removable chips, and a results table that handles its own loading, empty and error states.                                              |
| Page states            | Any view, panel, drawer or card whose content comes from an async source (HTTP, a resource, a signal store).                                              | Every region that loads data has four states — loading, loaded, empty and error. Design all four from the start so a screen never shows a blank box or a frozen spinner.                                                |
